name: Biodiversity net gain: nationally significant infrastructure projects
fact: Defra's June 2026 collection states BNG becomes mandatory for NSIP DCO applications made on or after 2 November 2026, with at least 10% BNG required.
gate: Do not apply NSIP BNG rules to an earlier DCO application or treat a future statutory start date as current compliance evidence.

name: What to include in biodiversity net gain baselines for NSIPs
fact: Published 2 June 2026, the guidance requires NSIP baselines to use the statutory biodiversity metric and sets evidence rules for habitats included or excluded from the pre-development baseline.
gate: A baseline calculation is not the final BNG outcome, consent decision or proof that mitigation/compensation is legally secured.

name: Using the nutrient neutrality calculators
fact: Natural England guidance updated 11 March 2026 describes nutrient budgets for residential development in 27 catchments and records March 2026 River Camel/River Eden catchment-boundary updates.
gate: A calculator output is an input to planning/Habitats Regulations evidence; it is not planning permission, HRA approval or secured mitigation.

name: Tools and resources for calculating nutrient neutrality
fact: Natural England's collection lists guidance and nutrient-neutrality calculators for 27 specific catchments.
gate: Use the calculator for the exact current catchment and version; collection membership alone does not establish a site's nutrient requirement.

name: Natural England's nutrient mitigation scheme for developers
fact: Updated 15 June 2026, the scheme allows eligible developments in the Tees and Poole Harbour catchments to apply for nutrient mitigation credits and notes that current calculator versions are required.
gate: Scheme eligibility or the ability to apply for credits is not a final nutrient certificate, planning permission or HRA conclusion.

name: Terms and conditions: nutrient mitigation scheme
fact: Updated 15 June 2026, the terms define provisional/final nutrient credit certificates, material-change duties, expiry rules and reservation of credits for the named development.
gate: A provisional certificate can expire and reserved credits can cease to be reserved; certificate state, development description and planning status must be current.

name: Poole Harbour catchment nutrient mitigation credits
fact: Current guidance says applicants need a planning application reference and the current Poole Harbour calculator to determine nitrogen-credit requirements, but planning permission is not required before applying for credits.
gate: A nutrient-credit application or provisional reservation is not planning permission, HRA approval or a final mitigation certificate.

name: Natural England nutrient mitigation scheme role clarification
fact: Natural England's 14 May 2026 update explains its statutory role in supporting sustainable development and nutrient-mitigation delivery while environmental-law compliance remains required.
gate: An official policy clarification is context, not evidence that a specific development has secured nutrient mitigation or passed HRA.

name: River Eden SAC nutrient neutrality calculator
fact: Updated 11 March 2026, the River Eden calculator reflects revised catchment boundaries and WINEP-related wastewater treatment assumptions.
gate: Use only for development within the current River Eden nutrient-neutrality catchment and re-run when assumptions or development details materially change.

name: River Camel SAC nutrient neutrality calculator
fact: Updated 11 March 2026, the River Camel calculator reflects revised catchment boundaries and WINEP treatment-work assumptions.
gate: A calculator result does not itself secure mitigation or prove the competent authority's Habitats Regulations conclusion.

name: The Broads and Wensum SACs nutrient neutrality calculator
fact: The current calculator combines The Broads and Wensum SAC catchments and reflects WINEP improvements and selected earlier permit-upgrade dates.
gate: Use the current merged calculator for the exact catchment; older River Wensum treatment must not be substituted.

name: River Mease SAC nutrient neutrality calculator
fact: The River Mease calculator reflects Water Industry Act duties, WINEP improvements and earlier completion dates for selected wastewater-treatment upgrades.
gate: Future treatment upgrades are model assumptions, not current site-specific nutrient mitigation already delivered.

name: Somerset Levels and Moors Ramsar nutrient neutrality calculator
fact: The calculator is the official nutrient-budget tool for proposed developments in the Somerset Levels and Moors Ramsar catchment and includes WINEP-related assumptions.
gate: Nutrient-budget calculation and mitigation security remain separate; catchment presence does not mean every development has the same nutrient requirement.

name: Solent nutrient neutrality calculator
fact: Natural England publishes the Solent nutrient-neutrality calculator reflecting wastewater-treatment duties announced in May 2024.
gate: Because calculator assumptions can be revised, verify the current version and local authority/Natural England advice before relying on an older result.

name: Protected sites and areas: how to review planning applications
fact: Natural England guidance requires authorities to check potential effects on SSSI, SAC, SPA and Ramsar sites, consult where required and undertake HRA for relevant European/Ramsar sites.
gate: A mapped overlap or proximity is a screening trigger, not an automatic refusal, approval or completed HRA conclusion.

name: Site of special scientific interest dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 4,128 SSSIs; collector last ran 20 July 2026 and the dataset includes some MHCLG-created data pending authoritative replacement.
gate: Dataset geometry is screening evidence; verify the exact Natural England designation, features, condition and Impact Risk Zone before parcel conclusions.

name: Sites of special scientific interest: condition and assessments
fact: Natural England's April 2026 guidance defines favourable, recovering, no-change, declining, part-destroyed and destroyed SSSI condition categories and the condition-improvement process.
gate: SSSI condition category is feature/site monitoring evidence, not permission for development or proof that impacts are acceptable.

name: Special area of conservation dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 260 SACs; collector last ran 18 July 2026, but newest data was found in September 2024 and some MHCLG-created data remains.
gate: Use as discovery/screening only; confirm current Natural England/JNCC designation and conservation objectives for exact HRA work.

name: Special protection area dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 88 SPAs; collector last ran 16 July 2026 and the dataset includes some MHCLG-created data pending replacement.
gate: SPA geometry is not an HRA conclusion; exact conservation objectives and likely-significant-effect assessment remain required.

name: Ramsar site dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 73 Ramsar sites; collector last ran 21 July 2026 and the dataset contains mixed authoritative/MHCLG-created provenance.
gate: Ramsar dataset intersection is a screening trigger, not evidence that the development is acceptable or unacceptable after assessment.

name: Ancient woodland dataset
fact: Planning Data reports 44,373 ancient woodlands from authoritative sources; collector last ran 22 July 2026 and newest data was found 21 March 2026.
gate: Inventory presence is strong screening evidence but smaller ancient woodlands may be absent and exact ecological/tree survey evidence remains required.

name: Ancient woodland, ancient trees and veteran trees planning advice
fact: Natural England and Forestry Commission standing advice treats ancient woodland and ancient/veteran trees as irreplaceable habitats and explains impact assessment, avoidance, mitigation, buffers and compensation as a last resort.
gate: Inventory absence does not prove no ancient habitat; fieldwork, local records and exact site assessment can still be required.

name: Local nature recovery strategies: areas and responsible authorities
fact: Defra's LNRS area/responsible-authority guidance was updated 26 June 2026 and identifies the statutory strategy geographies across England.
gate: Being within an LNRS area is not itself a biodiversity-unit uplift or planning constraint; use the adopted/current local strategy and exact mapped measure when assessing strategic significance.
